milestones.title: Article Fetch with Caching
milestones.vision: Add a new `article fetch [id]` command that fetches full article HTML from source URL, converts to markdown, displays in terminal, and caches the result in the database for subsequent views.
success_criteria: `article fetch [id]` command fetches full article HTML and converts to markdown
Markdown output is displayed directly in terminal
Database content field is updated after first fetch
Errors show clear, actionable messages (404, 403, timeout, conversion failure)
All tests pass and build succeeds

proof_strategy.riskOrUnknown: HTML-to-markdown conversion may fail on complex pages
proof_strategy.whatWillBeProven: FetchAndConvertArticle() handles malformed HTML and returns categorized errors
Database content field is updated after fetch, subsequent views show cached content

proof_strategy.riskOrUnknown: Real feeds may have edge cases (relative URLs, no URLs, JavaScript-rendered content)
proof_strategy.whatWillBeProven: Manual testing against 2-3 real RSS feeds succeeds with clear errors for unsupported formats

definition_of_done: Manual verification against real feeds passes

milestones.boundary_map_markdown:
## Boundary Map

### S01 → S02
Produces:
  converter.go → FetchAndConvertArticle(url string) (string, error)
  error categories → ErrCategoryConversionFailure, ErrCategoryEmptyContent

Consumes:
  fetcher.go → HTTP client pattern, HTTPError type
  htmltomarkdown library → Convert() function

### S01 → S03
Produces:
  converter.go → FetchAndConvertArticle() with error handling

Consumes:
  httptest → mock HTTP server for testing

### S02 → S03
Produces:
  article_fetch_cmd.go → article fetch [id] command

Consumes:
  converter.go → FetchAndConvertArticle()
  database/article.go → UpdateArticleContent() or similar

slices.goal: Add --open flag to article view command that opens the article URL in the default browser
Implement comprehensive error handling for network timeouts, HTTP errors (404, 403, 410), parse failures, empty content detection, and browser open failures with clear user-friendly messages

slices.title: HTML-to-markdown converter
slices.demo: FetchAndConvertArticle(url) fetches HTML from URL, converts to markdown, returns error with category for failures
slices.goal: Implement HTML-to-markdown converter with proper error handling
slices.success_criteria:
- FetchAndConvertArticle(url) returns markdown string on success
- Returns HTTPError with ErrCategoryNotFound for 404
- Returns HTTPError with ErrCategoryAccessDenied for 403
- Returns HTTPError with ErrCategoryTimeout for timeout
- Returns HTTPError with ErrCategoryConversionFailure for malformed HTML
- Returns HTTPError with ErrCategoryEmptyContent for empty result
- Unit tests pass for all error scenarios
slices.integration_closure: Converter function is tested with mock HTML and integrated with fetcher.go error patterns
slices.observability_impact: New error categories for conversion failures visible in error messages

slices.title: Article fetch command
slices.demo: article fetch [id] displays markdown in terminal and caches to database
slices.goal: Create article fetch command that fetches, converts, displays, and caches
slices.success_criteria:
- article fetch [id] command exists and accepts article ID
- Fetches full HTML from article Link URL
- Converts to markdown using FetchAndConvertArticle()
- Displays markdown in terminal (text mode) or JSON (json mode)
- Updates database content field after successful fetch
- Returns clear error messages on failure
slices.integration_closure: Command is wired to converter and database, end-to-end flow works
slices.observability_impact: New CLI command visible in help, database content field updated

slices.title: Tests and verification
slices.demo: All tests pass, manual verification against real feeds succeeds
slices.goal: Add tests and verify against real RSS feeds
slices.success_criteria:
- Unit tests for converter pass (converter_test.go)
- Integration tests with httptest server pass
- Manual testing against 2-3 real feeds succeeds
- Build succeeds (go build -o rss-cli ./cmd/rss-cli)
- All existing tests still pass (go test ./...)
slices.integration_closure: Tests cover all error scenarios, manual testing confirms real-world behavior
slices.observability_impact: Test coverage visible in go test output, manual test results documented

decisions.rationale: High-performance (Rust-based with Go bindings), preserves article structure, well-maintained, simple API
decisions.revisable: Yes — if CGO dependency causes cross-compilation issues

decisions.rationale: Cross-platform, simple API, handles OS-specific browser detection, well-established
decisions.revisable: Yes — if webbrowser has issues on target platforms

decisions.choice: Fetch full article content on-demand when viewing, not during feed update
decisions.rationale: Avoids storage bloat, always shows current content, respects publisher bandwidth, simpler implementation
decisions.revisable: Yes — if users report slow viewing experience

decisions.choice: Cache full article markdown in database content field after first fetch via article fetch command
decisions.rationale: User explicitly requested caching on first fetch. Reusing existing content field avoids schema migration. Supersedes D003 (no caching) for the new article fetch command.
